title: Claiming the first ragtime band on the street; Perkins as reader
summary: Laine says he had about the first ragtime band on the street; he recounts how his friend Perkins, a fine reader, came to play with him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Papa, do you have any idea when professional bands first started playing rags? When bands played the rags? Ragtimes, not rags. Ragtimes. Do you have any idea when they started playing rag times for money? No, I haven't.
Was that before you were born, do you think? No, I was playing music then. I had a ragtime band. And I'm about the first one that ever had a ragtime band on the street.

Is that right? That's correct. The first professional band? First, correct. That's correct. First one. Now, this Dave Perkins did not play ragtime. Dave Perkins did not play ragtime. Oh, yes. Dave played rag.
He used to mix this stuff up. Before you started playing? Oh, yeah. He played. Yeah, he played music. That's how I come to get Dave because Dave and I used to be pretty friends.

And he used to go see a lady in the block from me, you know. And he was always down by my house all the time. And he was a wonderful musician. Read music. Oh, that boy's heck of a sheet. And really just like nobody's business.
